comparison: Perfect agreement on SID-1::mCherry expression pattern (C81-C84). Both accept the imaging data showing developmental dynamics of the functional fusion protein without challenge.

Perfect agreement on SDG-1 response to perturbations in dsRNA processing (C124-C127). Both accept the data from crosses showing SDG-1 expression changes, though OpenEval notes the caveat about mating-induced artifacts.

Strong agreement on meta-analysis of published datasets (C97-C111). Both praise the genomic analysis showing sdg-1 regulation by RNA silencing pathways. OpenEval provides more detailed assessment of specific findings while peer reviewers treat this as a methodological strength.

Agreement on functional testing of SDG-1 (C128, C130). Both note the lack of effect on dsRNA-induced silencing. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a weakness in understanding mechanism but accept the data; OpenEval notes it suggests SDG-1 alone is insufficient.

Strong agreement on optogenetic approach (C67-C71). Both praise the temporal control method and accept the enhancement of silencing data. Peer reviewers highlight the 'robust neuronal stress model' while OpenEval notes appropriate controls and mechanistic consistency.

Agreement on temporal specificity of dsRNA transport (C58-C62, C64). Both accept the developmental window findings and RME-2 requirements. Peer reviewers treat this as part of 'valuable findings' while OpenEval provides detailed assessment of mechanistic support.

Agreement on identification of sid-1-dependent genes (C85-C86, C89, C93, C95-C96). Both accept the RNA-seq findings and transgenerational persistence. Peer reviewers emphasize the novelty of sdg-1 discovery while OpenEval notes the strong genetic evidence from multiple alleles.

Agreement on stochastic variation in sdg-1 expression (C53-C54). Both accept the variability between gonad arms and across generations. Peer reviewers note this as part of characterization while OpenEval emphasizes it supports the buffering model.

Agreement on dynamic nuclear localization of SDG-1 (C133-C136). Both accept the time-lapse imaging showing nuclear entry/exclusion. Peer reviewers treat this as part of molecular phenotype characterization while OpenEval discusses implications for additional roles.

Agreement on SDG-1 localization to perinuclear germ granules (C131-C132). Both accept colocalization with ZNFX-1. Peer review mentions 'SDG-2' which appears to be a typo for SDG-1. OpenEval notes the caveat about distinguishing specific interactions.

Agreement on substrate selectivity in dsRNA transport (C77-C80). Both accept the differential genetic requirements for short vs. mixed dsRNA. Peer reviewers praise the 'clever molecular genetic methods' while OpenEval notes the findings are well-documented but mechanistic basis requires investigation.

Agreement on sdg-1 genomic context (C115-C117). Both accept the retrotransposon location and lack of homologs. Peer reviewers find this discovery 'tantalizing' for regulatory loop models while OpenEval notes it suggests recent evolution.

Agreement on functional consequences of SID-1 loss (C55-C56). Both accept enhancement of mating-induced silencing and SDG-1's role. Peer reviewers treat this as part of the regulatory model while OpenEval emphasizes the clear demonstration of these effects.

Partial overlap on integrated model elements (C2, C46). Both accept the overall framework of dsRNA transport routes. OpenEval provides comprehensive assessment of the synthesized model while peer reviewers focus on the robustness of the experimental approach.

Partial overlap on model elements regarding substrate-specific mechanisms (C142-C145). Both accept these aspects of the integrated model. OpenEval treats them as well-supported synthesis while peer reviewers accept them as part of solid central findings.

Both address auto-inhibitory loop hypothesis (C7) but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model is speculative and requires direct evidence of retrotransposon activity effects. Peer reviewers also note uncertainty, calling it a 'tantalizing model' with unclear downstream mechanism, but don't reject it.

Partial overlap on SDG-1 localization aspects (C5, C50). OpenEval groups these with the auto-inhibitory loop hypothesis (rated UNCERTAIN). Peer reviewers accept the localization data as SUPPORTED but separate from the speculative regulatory model.

Partial overlap on retrotransposon context (C6, C49). OpenEval includes this in UNCERTAIN evaluation of auto-inhibitory loop. Peer reviewers accept the retrotransposon location as SUPPORTED finding that enables 'tantalizing models' requiring further investigation.

Partial overlap on sdg-1 expression variation (C121-C122). OpenEval includes stochastic variation in comprehensive characterization of sdg-1 genomic context and expression. Peer reviewers treat variability as part of overall characterization supporting the regulatory model.

OpenEval evaluates regulation of sdg-1 transcription (C138-C139), noting lack of transcriptional response to dsRNA and divergent effects in rde-4 mutants. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this fits within peer reviewers' general acceptance of thorough genetic characterization.

OpenEval provides comprehensive review of established knowledge and research gaps (C1, C8-C45) as context. No corresponding peer review result as this represents background rather than novel findings being evaluated.
